newsitem.title: UK: Capital Corp up on fresh bid talk. [CORRECTED 18:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Capital Corp up on fresh bid talk. [CORRECTED 18:51 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Capital Corporation Plc continued to rise on Thursday as speculation persisted of a second bid for the group.
The casino operator, already facing a bid from London Clubs International, added 10-1/2 pence to 212p on speculation of a rival offer from companies such as Ladbroke Group Plc or Rank Group.
"The market view is that there is going to be a counter bid, we just don't know at what level," said one market maker in Capital Corp stock.
"We've had a first bid on the table at 181p and the market thinks there could be another at 220p," he added.
The initial all-paper offer valued Capital Corp at 181 million pounds when tabled on February 17. Capital Corp has risen 40-1/2 pence or almost 24 percent since London Clubs made its offer.
Capital Corp chief executive Alan Hearn said recently that it had received inquiries from potential counter bidders but no direct approaches.

London Clubs had offered 47 new shares for every 100 Capital shares, a bid which Capital rejected saying it undervalued the company. London Clubs shares were 385p when the bid was tabled but have since fallen to 378.5p.
London Clubs is yet to send out the offer document and one analyst said it was waiting for Capital's 1996 results due on March 4.
Capital Corp owns and operates two casinos in the capital (corrects number of casinos owned and operated).
